extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for submitting, amending, and correcting drawings in U.S. patent applications (including timing, labeling, content, and examiner interactions), per MPEP and relevant 37 C.F.R. provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 1.84 (and international design rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to an application drawing must be in compliance with § 1.84 or, for a nonprovisional international design application, in compliance with §§ 1.84(c) and 1.1026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes must meet the technical and form requirements of § 1.84 (and § 1.1026 where applicable). This is the foundational requirement before any replacement or new sheets are accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use replacement sheets for amended drawings and label them
rubrics_metrics.description: All amended drawings must be submitted on a replacement sheet of drawings which shall be an attachment to the amendment document and, in the top margin, labeled "Replacement Sheet." Any new sheet of drawings containing an additional figure must be labeled in the top margin as "New Sheet."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each drawing sheet submitted after filing must be marked in the top margin as either "Replacement Sheet" or "New Sheet" pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sheet must include all figures from immediate prior version
rubrics_metrics.description: Any replacement sheet of drawings shall include all of the figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting a replacement sheet, include every figure that previously appeared on that sheet (do not submit only the amended figure alone on that sheet).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not label amended figures as "amended"
rubrics_metrics.description: The figure or figure number of the amended drawing(s) must not be labeled as "amended."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though a replacement sheet is provided, the actual figure labels/numbers should remain as originally numbered and not carry an "amended" mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain all drawing changes in amendment or remarks section
rubrics_metrics.description: All changes to the drawings shall be explained, in detail, in either the drawing amendment or remarks section of the amendment paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear explanation of what was changed and why in the amendment or remarks accompanying the replacement/new sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated (marked-up) sheet rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure, including annotations indicating the changes made, may be included. The marked-up copy must be clearly labeled as "Annotated Sheet" and must be presented in the amendment or remarks section that explains the change to the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotated sheets are optional unless required by the examiner. If provided or required, label them "Annotated Sheet" and include them within the amendment/remarks that explain the changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require annotated drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure, including annotations indicating the changes made, must be provided when required by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner requests an annotated/marked-up sheet, the applicant must supply it as part of the amendment/remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility: USPTO does not make drawing changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office does not make drawing changes. It is applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the drawings are corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph guidance to be used by examiners when applicants ask the Office to make drawing changes. Applicants must follow the procedures and correct drawings themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying indicia on drawing sheets (if provided)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia, if provided, should include the title of the invention, inventor’s name, and application number, or docket number (if any) if an application number has not been assigned to the application. If this information is provided, it must be placed on the front of each sheet and within the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place identifying information in the top margin/front of each sheet if included; this aids handling but is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will not release drawings for purposes of correction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not release drawings for purposes of correction. If corrections are necessary, new corrected drawings must be submitted within the time set by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect the Office to physically alter or return original drawings for you to correct; instead submit new corrected sheets within the deadline set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: corrections must be filed within set time or application abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is required to submit acceptable corrected drawings within the time period set in the Office action. Failure to take corrective action within the set period will result in ABANDONMENT of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely response is mandatory. The Office sets the time in its action; follow it exactly to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Allowability: three-month shortened period for corrected drawings (no extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a corrected drawing is required or if a drawing does not comply with § 1.84 or an amended drawing submitted under § 1.121(d) in a nonprovisional international design application does not comply with § 1.1026 at the time an application is allowed, the Office may notify the applicant in a notice of allowability and set a three-month period of time from the mail date of the notice of allowability within which the applicant must file a corrected drawing in compliance with § 1.84 or 1.1026, as applicable, to avoid abandonment. This time period is not extendable under § 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections required at allowance must be filed within the three-month shortened statutory period in the Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37); extensions under § 1.136 are not available for this filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings filed after application placed on files generally not published
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in § 1.215(c), any patent application publication will not include drawings filed after the application has been placed on the files for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To have drawings included in the published application, submit them before the application is placed on the files for examination or rely on limited exceptions under § 1.215(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to drawings will not be held in abeyance
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless applicant is otherwise notified in an Office action, objections to the drawings in a utility or plant application will not be held in abeyance, and a request to hold objections to the drawings in abeyance will not be considered a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action (§ 1.135(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should correct drawing objections promptly rather than requesting abeyance; such requests generally will not be accepted and may affect prosecution posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design application exception for reproducible drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a drawing in a design application meets the requirements of § 1.84(e), (f), and (g) and is suitable for reproduction, but is not otherwise in compliance with § 1.84, the drawing may be admitted for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications have limited flexibility: if the drawing is reproducible and meets certain subparagraphs, it may be admitted despite other technical noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of canceled figures requires specification amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: A canceled figure may be reinstated. An amendment should be made to the specification adding the brief description of the view if a canceled figure is reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reinstating a canceled figure, also amend the specification to add the brief description of that view so the reinstatement is reflected in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner notification and next Office action if changes not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the changes to the drawing figure(s) are not accepted by the examiner, applicant will be notified of any required corrective action in the next Office action. No further drawing submission will be required, unless applicant is notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner rejects the presented drawing changes, they will identify required corrections in the next Office action; do not submit further changes unless the Office requests them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendment involving drawing changes: applicant must implement agreed changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The following changes to the drawings have been approved by the examiner and agreed upon by applicant: [1]. In order to avoid abandonment of the application, applicant must make these agreed upon drawing changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the examiner and applicant agree to drawing changes via an Examiner’s Amendment, the applicant must effect those agreed changes (and follow form paragraph sequencing such as including 6.39 and 6.40).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph guidance to inform applicants about how to effect drawing changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 6.39 – USPTO Does Not Make Drawing Changes; ¶ 6.40 – Information on How To Effect Drawing Changes; ¶ 6.41 and ¶ 6.42 reminders; ¶ 6.43 Drawings Contain Informalities, Application Allowed) provide standardized examiner wording to notify applicants of drawing corrections and required procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should use these standardized form paragraphs to communicate that applicants must correct drawings, instructions on replacement/annotated sheets, timing, and consequences of failing to correct drawings.
